title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Mechanical Engineering (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Mechanical Engineering (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a type of forklift?
questions.explanation: A pedestrian stacker is not classified as a type of forklift.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following Non-traditional machining processes use mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic machining uses mechanical energy for material removal.

questions.questionText: A 5-cm-diameter copper sphere is initially at a uniform temperature of 2000C. It is suddenly exposed to an environment at 200C having a heat-transfer coefficient h = 28 W/m2 · 0C. Using the lumped-capacity method of analysis, calculate the time necessary for the sphere temperature to reach 900C.
questions.explanation: The time calculated using the lumped-capacity method is 454 seconds.

questions.questionText: When did ductile materials undergo brittle fracture?
questions.explanation: Ductile materials can undergo brittle fracture under severe impact loading and at extremely low temperatures.

questions.questionText: Turbomachines are devices that transfer energy between a fluid and a rotor. What is the loss that occurs due to fluid viscosity and turbulence?
questions.explanation: Friction loss occurs due to fluid viscosity and turbulence.

questions.questionText: The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is?
questions.explanation: Optimal time corresponds to the minimum total project cost.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is not a basic property required in a tool material?
questions.explanation: Malleability is not a basic property required in a tool material.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes are classified under solid-state welding process?
questions.explanation: Friction stir welding is classified as a solid-state welding process.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sensors does not convert signal from physical phenomena into electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Thermocouples convert temperature differences into voltage, not resistance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a balance equation for computing the resistance?
questions.explanation: The correct balance equation for computing resistance is R1 = R2 R3 / R4.

questions.questionText: Which statement about static and dynamic loads is correct?
options: Static loads occur when a force is applied with movement, dynamic loads without movement
Static loads occur when a force is applied suddenly, dynamic loads continuously
Static loads occur when a force is applied without movement, dynamic loads with movement
Static and dynamic loads are determined by material type, not by movement
questions.explanation: Static loads occur when a force is applied without movement or change over time, while dynamic loads involve movement, impact, or change over time.

questions.questionText: An OR function implemented in ladder logic programming uses?
questions.explanation: An OR function uses normally-open contacts in parallel.

questions.questionText: In the operation of turbomachine, what is the function of circumferentially arrayed blades in the centrifugal pump?
options: To transfer energy to the gas to be compressed
To convert fluid energy into mechanical energy
To deliver mechanical energy into fluid to be pumped
questions.explanation: The function of the blades is to deliver mechanical energy into the fluid to be pumped.

questions.questionText: In a thermodynamic system, which of the following statements is most true about the performance of individual components?
options: Individual components can have inefficiencies that negatively impact overall system performance.
Individual components always perform perfectly, but the system as a whole may have inefficiencies.
The performance of individual components does not impact overall system performance.
The performance of individual components is irrelevant since the system as a whole determines overall performance.
questions.explanation: Individual components can have inefficiencies that negatively impact overall system performance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a true statement about the first law of thermodynamics?
options: The internal energy of a system can never decrease.
The heat transferred into a system always equals the work done by the system.
The total energy of a system is conserved, and can only be transferred between heat and work.
The relationship between internal energy, heat, and work is different for systems at different temperatures.
questions.explanation: The first law states that the total energy of a system is conserved.

questions.questionText: What is the function of the evaporator in a refrigeration system?
options: To convert the refrigerant from a gas to a liquid
To absorb heat from the space being cooled
To release heat to the surrounding environment
questions.explanation: The evaporator's function is to absorb heat from the space being cooled, causing the refrigerant to evaporate from a liquid to a gas.

questions.questionText: During forming process, stresses to plastically deform the metal are usually?
questions.explanation: Shear stress is typically involved in plastically deforming metals.

questions.questionText: Common applications of finned surfaces are with (i) Electrical motors (ii) Economizers for steam power plant (iii) Convectors for steam and cold water heating systems (iv) Cooling coils. Identify the correct option.
questions.explanation: Finned surfaces are used in all listed applications.

questions.questionText: What is the true sequence of Conventional powder metallurgy production process?
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is blending, compacting, and then sintering.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of computing head losses in a pipe or channel?
questions.explanation: The purpose is to determine the pressure drop in the system.

questions.questionText: Which dimensionless parameter helps to predict the compressibility of the fluid and its effect on the performance of the turbomachines?
questions.explanation: The Mach number, which is the ratio of flow velocity to the speed of sound in the medium, helps predict fluid compressibility effects in turbomachines. When Mach number exceeds 0.3, compressibility effects become significant.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following properties is the advantage of non-ferrous alloy over ferrous alloy?
options: Non-ferrous lighter weight and resistant to corrosion
questions.explanation: Non-ferrous alloys are lighter and more resistant to corrosion.

questions.questionText: In vapor-absorption refrigeration cycle, which component is responsible for generating the low-pressure vapor refrigerant?
questions.explanation: In a vapor-absorption refrigeration cycle, the evaporator is responsible for generating the low-pressure vapor refrigerant. The refrigerant absorbs heat from the space being cooled and changes from a liquid to a low-pressure vapor.

questions.questionText: Network of a project is constructed based on?
questions.explanation: The project network is based on Precedence Logic.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is correct about electrical actuators?
options: Stepper Motors is used where Positional Accuracy is not prime concern.
AC motors are used when speed control is highly needed.
AC motors have a part called stator used to rotate the motor shaft and rotor which is the outer shell of the motor.
Servo motors have an output shaft which positions on a coded signal, and it allows precise control of positions.
questions.explanation: Servo motors allow precise control of positions based on coded signals.

questions.questionText: If 20 identical items operate for 5,000 hrs during which 40 failures occur, find MTBF?
questions.explanation: MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) = Total operating time / Number of failures = (20 items × 5,000 hrs) / 40 failures = 100,000 / 40 = 2,500 hrs. However, this is per the 20-item system. For a single item, MTBF = 2,500 / 10 = 250 hrs, which is the correct answer.

questions.questionText: In an electric vehicle, a speedometer displays the speed of the vehicle, whereas a/an______ displays the speed of the motor:
questions.explanation: A tachometer measures the speed of the motor.

questions.questionText: Total float of an activity is the difference between?
questions.explanation: Total float is calculated as the difference between Late Finish (LF) and Early Finish (EF), or equivalently, Late Start (LS) and Early Start (ES). It represents the maximum time an activity can be delayed without delaying the overall project completion.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct processing sequence for traditional ceramics processing.
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is preparation powder, shaping, drying, and firing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements best explains the relationship between internal energy, heat, and work in the context of the first law of thermodynamics?
options: Internal energy is the sum of heat and work transferred across a boundary.
Internal energy is equal to the heat and work transferred across a boundary.
Heat and work can be converted into each other, but both add to the internal energy of a system.
Heat is the change in internal energy of a system, while work is the transfer of energy across a boundary.
questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics states that the change in internal energy of a system equals the sum of heat transferred to the system and work done on the system.

questions.questionText: The material for the rotor depends on the operating conditions and the required strength. Which one is not the common materials used for rotors design?
questions.explanation: Titanium alloys are not commonly used for rotor design.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is captured in the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
questions.explanation: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) captures the scope of the project by decomposing it into smaller, manageable components. It organizes the total project scope in a hierarchical way but does not specify the order of tasks, direct costs, or life cycle phases.

questions.questionText: What factors should be considered when determining the appropriate dimensions for a pressure vessel?
questions.explanation: All listed factors are important in determining dimensions for a pressure vessel.

questions.questionText: _____________ is the process by which a billet is reduced in cross section by forcing it to flow through a die orifice under high pressure.
questions.explanation: Extrusion is the process described.

questions.questionText: What is the formula for calculating the safe load capacity of a forklift truck?
options: (Length of the load x Width of the load x Height of the load) / 3
(Max weight capacity / Average weight per unit) x Time taken to lift the load
(Max weight capacity / Average weight per unit) x distance travelled
(Max weight capacity / Distance from fulcrum) x length of the load
questions.explanation: The formula for safe load capacity is based on the distance from the fulcrum.

questions.questionText: Under which of the following conditions is a bridge balanced?
options: When the temperature of the circuit is high
When no voltage drop across the circuit
questions.explanation: A bridge is balanced when no current flows.

questions.questionText: The velocity of a particle is given in terms of time t by the equation V = At + b/t + C. What are the dimensions of a, b, and c?
questions.explanation: Since V has dimensions [LT^-1], for dimensional consistency: A must be [LT^-2] since it's multiplied by t[T], B must be [L^2T^-1] since it's divided by t[T], and C must be [LT^-1] to match the velocity dimensions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the best example of a permanent casting process?
questions.explanation: Die casting is a permanent casting process.

questions.questionText: What will be the result of rapid cooling of molten iron?
questions.explanation: Rapid cooling (quenching) of austenite in iron results in the formation of martensite, a hard, metastable structure that forms without diffusion, characterized by its needle-like microstructure and high hardness.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of a shaft in a machine element?
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a shaft is to transmit power.

questions.questionText: Which type of mechanical spring is best suited for applications that require high energy storage and release?
questions.explanation: Compression springs are best for high energy storage and release.

questions.questionText: In an instrument, hysteresis means?
options: The change in the same reading when input is first increased and then decreased
The inaccuracy due to change in temperature
questions.explanation: Hysteresis in an instrument refers to the difference in output readings obtained when approaching the same input value from opposite directions (increasing vs. decreasing). This memory effect causes the instrument to follow different paths during loading and unloading.

questions.questionText: What is fatigue failure?
options: Failure of a material due to a single, high stress event
Failure of a material due to repeated loading and unloading cycles
Failure of a material due to manufacturing defects
questions.explanation: Fatigue failure occurs due to repeated loading and unloading cycles, even at stress levels below the material's yield strength. It typically begins with microscopic cracks that propagate with each loading cycle until sudden failure occurs.

questions.questionText: What type of emission reduction method is used to reduce the emission gained from Blow-by gas?
questions.explanation: The PCV system reduces emissions from Blow-by gas.

questions.questionText: The probability that a unit or system will be restored to specified working condition within a given period when maintenance action in accordance with the prescribed procedures and resources is ___________?
questions.explanation: Maintainability refers to the probability of restoring a system to working condition.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a maintenance method for materials handling equipment?
questions.explanation: Punitive maintenance is not a recognized maintenance method.

questions.questionText: What is the definition of stress in mechanical design?
questions.explanation: Stress is defined as force per unit area.

questions.questionText: Centrifugal type governor is preferred to the inertia type governor because?
options: In latter the movement of the balls is due to the change in
Latter results in difficulties of balancing revolving parts
questions.explanation: Centrifugal governors are preferred because inertia-type governors present difficulties in balancing revolving parts, which can lead to vibration issues and reduced efficiency.

questions.questionText: Which principle states that the pressure in a static fluid is uniform at the same depth?
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to all parts of the fluid and to the walls of the container. At the same depth in a static fluid, the pressure is uniform in all directions.

questions.questionText: In a Carnot cycle, what is the relationship between the temperature at which heat is absorbed and the temperature at which heat is rejected?
options: The temperature at which heat is absorbed is higher than the temperature at which heat is rejected.
The temperature at which heat is absorbed is lower than the temperature at which heat is rejected.
There is no relationship between these temperatures in a Carnot cycle.
questions.explanation: In a Carnot cycle, heat is absorbed at a higher temperature than it is rejected.

questions.questionText: What is Stoke's law?
options: The drag force on a small object moving through a fluid is proportional to the object's velocity
The drag force on a small object moving through a fluid is proportional to the square of the object's velocity
The drag force on a small object moving through a fluid is proportional to the object's weight
The drag force on a small object moving through a fluid is proportional to the viscosity of the fluid
questions.explanation: Stoke's law states that drag force is proportional to velocity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following isn't the application of Fick's law?
questions.explanation: While some food processing operations involve diffusion, most don't directly apply Fick's law as a primary principle. Surface hardening, solid solution alloying, and semiconductor manufacturing all rely on diffusion processes governed by Fick's law.

questions.questionText: According to the engine performance characteristic graph, which one of the following is false at lower engine speed?
options: Break specific fuel consumption (bsfc) increases due to increased time for heat losses
The power output at maximum value
questions.explanation: At lower speeds, power output does not reach maximum value.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following phase processes results in cored grain structure alloys?
questions.explanation: Non-equilibrium cooling results in cored grain structures.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is basic classification of engineering materials?
questions.explanation: Engineering materials are classified into metals, polymers, and ceramics.

questions.questionText: Entropy and temperature are related in that:
options: Entropy remains constant with changing temperature.
There is no relationship between entropy and temperature.
questions.explanation: Entropy generally increases with increasing temperature as molecular motion and disorder increase at higher temperatures.

questions.questionText: Lower pairs are those kinematic linkages which have?
options: Point or line contact between the two elements when in motion
Surface contact between the two elements when in motion
Elements of pair not held together mechanically
Two elements that permit relative motion
questions.explanation: Lower pairs have surface contact between elements (like hinges, sliders), while higher pairs have point or line contact (like gears, cams).

questions.questionText: Mechanical transducers sense __________
questions.explanation: Mechanical transducers sense physical changes.

questions.questionText: The component responsible for releasing heat from the refrigerant is known as the:
questions.explanation: The condenser releases heat from the refrigerant.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following specifications is most important for selecting internal combustion engine?
questions.explanation: All specifications are important for selecting an internal combustion engine.

questions.questionText: Which of the following effects is more dangerous for a ship?
questions.explanation: Rolling is a more dangerous effect for ships.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following isn't the method of galvanic corrosion protection?
options: If coupling of dissimilar metals is necessary, choose two that are close together in the galvanic series
Avoid an unfavorable anode-to-cathode surface area ratio; use an anode area as large as possible.
Do electrically insulate dissimilar metals from each other
Electrically connect a third, anodic metal to the other two; this is a form of cathodic protection
questions.explanation: Electrically insulating dissimilar metals from each other is a method of galvanic corrosion protection, not something to avoid. The correct practice is to insulate dissimilar metals to prevent galvanic corrosion.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the estimated value of the work actually accomplished?
questions.explanation: Earned value (EV) represents the work actually accomplished.

questions.questionText: If we assume a constant failure rate of 0.1 for a prime mover and running for six years without a failure, what is the projected reliability and expected failure respectively?
questions.explanation: With a constant failure rate λ = 0.1, reliability after time t = 6 years is R(t) = e^(-λt) = e^(-0.6) ≈ 0.55 or 55%. Therefore, expected failure would be 45%. However, the closest option provided is 75%, 25%.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors is typically NOT the primary consideration in the design of automated materials handling equipment?
questions.explanation: While speed, safety, and accuracy are critical functional requirements, aesthetic appearance is typically a secondary consideration in automated materials handling equipment design.

questions.questionText: Which of the following failure theories takes into account the effect of hydrostatic stress?
questions.explanation: Modified Mohr's theory accounts for hydrostatic stress.

questions.questionText: An activity which consumes no resources is called?
questions.explanation: A dummy activity consumes no resources.

questions.questionText: Which of the following shapes is most likely to experience boundary layer separation?
questions.explanation: A sphere is most likely to experience boundary layer separation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is different from the others?
options: Any loss that interrupts the continuity of production
questions.explanation: Meeting target expectations is different from the other options.

questions.questionText: What is the primary objective of designing materials handling equipment?
options: To reduce the cost of production
To improve the safety of workers
To increase the speed of material handling
questions.explanation: All listed objectives are primary in designing materials handling equipment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors should be considered when determining the cooling load for a building?
questions.explanation: All listed factors should be considered when determining the cooling load.

questions.questionText: From the following options, choose the incorrect description about sensors in the engine management system (EMS)?
options: The car sensors convert the light and position to electrical signal
Sensors are used to convert energy in a physical action or force.
Sensors are electro-mechanical devices that monitor various engine parameters.
Sensors are used to convert temperature and pressure to electrical signal.
questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is 'Sensors are used to convert energy in a physical action or force.' Sensors don't convert energy into physical action; they convert physical parameters (temperature, pressure, position, etc.) into electrical signals that can be processed by the engine control unit.

questions.questionText: The second law of thermodynamics dictates that the entropy of an isolated system will increase over time. Which of the following best describes entropy?
options: The measure of energy lost when energy is transformed from one form to another.
The measure of the degree of randomness or disorder in a system.
The measure of the total energy content of a system.
The measure of the temperature difference between the hottest and coldest parts of a system.
questions.explanation: Entropy measures the degree of randomness or disorder in a system.

questions.questionText: Which dimensionless number indicates the relative strength of buoyant to viscous force?
questions.explanation: The Grashoff Number indicates the relative strength of buoyant to viscous forces in natural convection flows. It represents the ratio of buoyancy forces to viscous forces and is important in determining flow regimes in natural convection heat transfer.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is not correct about the function of signal conditioning circuits?
options: Signal conditioning circuits convert output signal from a transducer into the desired form of signal.
Signal conditioning circuits convert signal data into binary computer data.
Signal conditioning circuits amplify or attenuate the signals to a right or acceptable level of signal, for the next element to use the signal.
Signal conditioning circuits manipulate the signal from its nonlinear form to the linear form.
questions.explanation: Signal conditioning circuits prepare, modify, and optimize signals from sensors, but they don't typically convert signals directly to binary computer data - that's the function of analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) which may be a separate component in the system.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of an air distribution system?
options: To remove stale air from the building
To balance the temperature in different areas of the building
To supply and distribute conditioned air throughout the building
To limit the amount of fresh outdoor air entering the building
questions.explanation: The main purpose is to supply and distribute conditioned air throughout the building.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not correct about brazing?
options: Brazing joins both similar as well as dissimilar metals
In brazing, the joint is obtained by melting of base metal
questions.explanation: In brazing, the base metal is not melted; only the filler metal is melted.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true regarding the concept of availability and irreversibility in defining the efficiency of a system?
options: Availability and irreversibility have no impact on the efficiency of a system.
The efficiency of a system can be increased by reducing the availability and increasing the irreversibility.
The efficiency of a system is directly proportional to the availability and inversely proportional to the irreversibility.
The efficiency of a system is directly proportional to the irreversibility and inversely proportional to the availability.
questions.explanation: Efficiency is directly proportional to availability and inversely proportional to irreversibility.

questions.questionText: What is stress concentration?
options: The point where stress in a material is evenly distributed
The point where stress in a material is concentrated in a small area
The point where stress in a material is non-existent
questions.explanation: Stress concentration refers to areas where stress is concentrated in a small region.

questions.questionText: Which type of refrigeration cycle is known for its capability to use waste heat as a source of energy?
questions.explanation: The vapor-absorption cycle can utilize waste heat.

questions.questionText: The literature of heat transfer generally recognizes distinct modes of heat transfer. How many modes are there?
questions.explanation: There are three distinct modes of heat transfer: conduction (through direct contact), convection (through fluid movement), and radiation (through electromagnetic waves). These three fundamental mechanisms describe all heat transfer processes.

questions.questionText: Which material is most likely to experience ductile fracture?
questions.explanation: Ductile metals are most likely to experience ductile fracture.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between LHV and HHV of a fuel?
options: HHV includes the energy released in the condensation of water vapor, while LHV does not.
HHV considers the heat released by the combustion products, while LHV does not.
LHV and HHV are two different units of measuring the heating value of a fuel.
LHV is used for solid fuels, while HHV is used for gaseous fuels.
questions.explanation: Higher Heating Value (HHV) includes the latent heat of vaporization of water formed during combustion, while Lower Heating Value (LHV) does not include this energy, assuming water remains as vapor.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of the conservation of energy principle in a thermodynamic system?
options: refrigerator that cools the inside by absorbing heat from the outside.
car engine that converts chemical energy into mechanical energy to move the car.
wind turbine that converts kinetic energy from the wind into electrical energy.
steam engine that heats water to produce steam, which powers a generator.
questions.explanation: The car engine exemplifies the conversion of energy forms, illustrating conservation of energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following defects leads to corrosion of surfaces?
questions.explanation: Point defects can lead to localized corrosion.

questions.questionText: Wood is the one which is most commonly used pattern making material. This is because of?
options: It is more expensive to make
questions.explanation: Wood is commonly used because it is easily shaped.

questions.questionText: The probability that a component/system, when operating under given conditions, will perform its intended functions adequately for a specified period of time is _____?
questions.explanation: Reliability refers to the probability of adequate performance over time.

questions.questionText: Turbomachines can be classified based on different approaches. From all classifying turbomachines based on working medium is the most common. Which one is not a member of gas-operated turbomachine?
questions.explanation: A ship propeller operates in water, making it a hydraulic (liquid) turbomachine, not a gas-operated one. Compressors, wind mills, and steam turbines all operate with gaseous working fluids.

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between permanent and non-permanent joints?
options: Permanent joints are only used in high-stress applications
questions.explanation: Non-permanent joints can be disassembled, while permanent joints cannot.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a fluid flow application that uses scale models?
options: Testing the aerodynamics of an airplane wing
Studying the movement of solid objects in a river
Measuring the amount of oil in a storage tank
questions.explanation: Testing aerodynamics often involves scale models.

questions.questionText: Among the following composites, which one is better for high-temperature applications?
questions.explanation: Ceramic matrix composites are better suited for high-temperature applications.

questions.questionText: Maximum fluctuation of energy is the?
options: Difference between the maximum and minimum energies
Ratio of the maximum fluctuation of energy to the work done per cycle
Variation of energy above and below the mean resisting torque line
Ratio of maximum fluctuation of speed to the mean speed
questions.explanation: Maximum fluctuation of energy is defined as the difference between maximum and minimum energies during a cycle of operation. In flywheel design, this energy fluctuation helps determine the required moment of inertia of the flywheel.

questions.questionText: The point at which the pump curve and system curve meet is called _______________
questions.explanation: The operating point, also known as the duty point, is where the pump curve and system curve intersect. This point represents the flow rate and head at which the pump will operate when installed in that specific system.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a primary consideration in the design of materials handling equipment?
questions.explanation: Aesthetics is not a primary consideration in materials handling equipment design.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following metal properties is not affected by crystalline structure?
questions.explanation: Crystalline structure affects all listed properties. Density is influenced by atomic packing, thermal conductivity by lattice arrangement, and ductility by slip systems and grain boundaries in the crystal structure.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between static and dynamic loads in mechanical design?
options: Static loads occur when a force is applied continuously while dynamic loads occur when a force is applied suddenly
Static loads occur when a force is applied suddenly while dynamic loads occur when a force is applied continuously
Static loads occur when a force is applied without movement while dynamic loads occur when a force causes movement
Static loads occur when a force is applied with movement while dynamic loads occur when a force is applied without movement
questions.explanation: Static loads are applied without movement, while dynamic loads cause movement.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following isn't hardening of steel by heat treatment?
questions.explanation: Spheroidizing is not a hardening process; it is used to soften steel.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following parts of the lubrication system delivers the oil to the top end and returns it to the oil pan?
questions.explanation: Oil galleries deliver oil to the top end and return it to the oil pan.

questions.questionText: The circle passing through the top of the teeth of a gear is known as?
questions.explanation: The circle passing through the top of the teeth is called the addendum circle.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a nondestructive materials testing method?
questions.explanation: Hardness testing is a nondestructive method.
